radiology_report:
Subject: Prostate Multiparametric MRI | Facility: Amsterdam UMC, VUmc campus | Scan Date: 28 January 2025

Clinical Indication: A 63-year-old gentleman presents for lesion characterization and PI-RADS scoring, driven by a PSA value of 6.4 ng/mL alongside a previously positive biopsy bucket.

FINDINGS:
The gland occupies 41.62 mL. T2-weighted sequences show a largely intact peripheral zone, interrupted only by a discrete hypointense focus within the left mid-gland sector, spanning approximately 11 x 9 x 10 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging highlights pronounced restriction here, mirrored by corresponding ADC hypointensity. Post-contrast phases capture early, focal enhancement against the background parenchyma. The transition zone exhibits mild nodular hyperplasia devoid of suspicious architecture. Seminal vesicles remain clear. No extraprostatic extension or suspicious lymphadenopathy is detected.

IMPRESSION:
Focal lesion in the left mid-gland peripheral zone consistent with PI-RADS 4.
Prostate volume 41.62 mL; PSA density 0.154 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.80504376.

previous_notes.author: Dr. T. Hendriks (GP)
previous_notes.text: 11 Aug 2023 - Dr. T. Hendriks (GP): The gentleman attended for routine monitoring of his gradually ascending PSA trajectory. Recent laboratory results indicate a value of 2.6 ng/mL, representing an upward shift from his established baseline. Given his age and the consistent rise, a urology referral has been arranged for a thorough workup, including potential imaging and tissue sampling. Lower urinary tract symptoms have remained unchanged, and his daily walking routine continues uneventfully.
